p.i: Admodum in turbidis Gracia Concionibus ve-nalis orator. Scilicet illud est Deum suo ho-nore & providentia communis & gratia deturbare, homines etiam cum dispendio salutis & solatii intumidare, nixos in vanum prædicatis falso liberi arbitrij facultatibus aut etiam Communi gratia quā fallax & inefficax, multos, quibus contigit, in cœno destituit. Hoc est pietatem & religionem in exilium agere, dum homines docentur semet potius suasque opes respicere & conando agendoque eniti, quàm supplicus[?] muliebribus, reflexisque in Deum cordibus, ejus auxilium implorare.

Adeo universam Theologiam non turbant, sed exturbant novi dogmatistæ, fabri ψευδῶν[?] δο-ξῶν[?] vere παραδόξων[?], quas, ut tueantur[?], in omnes se formas vertere, modo Scriptura dicta planissima & evidentissimos S. S. sensus torquendo eludere, modo philosophiam advocare, ut qui propter habitum mentes suas in Scripturis subegissent, nec offusis nebulis à tramite recto in pravum abduci possent, acumine spinarum rationis humanæ punctì[?] aut sinuosis anfractibus exotica sapientia turbati de via veritate dubitare inciperent. page.notes: Running head read as printed: "Præfatio ad Lectorem." Greek words in the second paragraph are uncertain and marked [?]: "ψευδῶν", "δοξῶν" and "παραδόξων" are my best reading of the printed letters. "tueantur" (printed as possibly "tneantur") and "supplicus" are doubtful. "punctì" is doubtful. The spelling "Gracia" is copied as printed. No page number or signature is visible. The catchword "ni-" is the first syllable of the next page.
